question: In which year did Henry Moseley use X-rays to measure the wavelength of elements, and correlate these measurements with their atomic numbers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1913**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Moseley**, an English physicist, used **X-ray spectroscopy** in **1913** to measure the wavelengths of X-rays emitted by elements.
 
• Moseley discovered that these wavelengths were correlated with the **atomic number** of each element rather than their atomic weight.
 
• This groundbreaking work led to the modern understanding of the **periodic table**, reorganizing elements based on their atomic numbers rather than atomic masses.
 
• Moseley formulated the concept of **Moseley's Law**, which states that the square root of the frequency of emitted X-rays is proportional to the atomic number.
 
• This study established the **atomic number** as a fundamental property of elements, marking a significant advancement in atomic physics and chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Moseley’s Contributions:**

 
 
• Moseley’s work provided clarity in the arrangement of elements in the **periodic table**, identifying gaps where undiscovered elements should be placed.
 
• His research directly influenced the discovery of new elements such as **technetium (atomic number 43)** and **promethium (atomic number 61)**.
 
• Moseley’s findings resolved inconsistencies in the earlier classification, where elements like iodine and tellurium were misplaced due to reliance on atomic weights.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Moseley’s Law:**
 
 
• Moseley’s Law is used in **X-ray crystallography** to analyze the structure of materials and identify elements.
 
• It is widely employed in **scientific and industrial fields**, including material science and analytical chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Moseley conducted his research during the early 20th century, a period marked by significant advancements in quantum physics and atomic theory.
 
• His work complemented the discoveries of other scientists like **Dmitri Mendeleev**, who initially proposed the periodic table based on atomic weights.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Moseley’s untimely death in **World War I** in 1915 at the age of 27 was a great loss to the scientific community.
 
• His contributions are remembered as a foundational step in the development of **modern atomic theory**.
 
• The atomic numbers identified by Moseley remain fundamental in **element classification** and periodic table organization.
